formats.key: PermitWitnessTransferFrom(TokenPermissions permitted,address spender,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline,DutchOrder witness)DutchOrder(OrderInfo info,uint256 decayStartTime,uint256 decayEndTime,address inputToken,uint256 inputStartAmount,uint256 inputEndAmount,DutchOutput[] outputs)DutchOutput(address token,uint256 startAmount,uint256 endAmount,address recipient)OrderInfo(address reactor,address swapper,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline,address additionalValidationContract,bytes additionalValidationData)TokenPermissions(address token,uint256 amount)
effects: The signer lets the spender (the UniswapX reactor) pull permitted.token from the signer's wallet once through Permit2, up to permitted.amount.
The amount actually pulled is the decayed input amount at fill time, between inputStartAmount and inputEndAmount; the reactor sets permitted.amount to inputEndAmount, the maximum.
The pulled input tokens go to the filler, not to a fixed address in the message.
Each output pays its token (native currency when the token is the zero address) to its recipient. The amount decays from startAmount down to endAmount, so at least endAmount arrives.
Outputs can go to recipients other than the signer, for example interface fee outputs.
The Permit2 unordered nonce is used. The order can be filled only until the earlier of deadline and info.deadline.
The additionalValidationContract can stop a fill (for example to limit fillers). It moves none of the signer's assets.
formats.shown: Intent 'UniswapX Dutch Order' with the raw spender, the Permit2 amount, the input start amount as 'Spend max', each output's end amount as 'Minimum amounts to receive' with its raw recipient, and the permit deadline.

findings.title: Dutch order 'Spend max' shows inputStartAmount, but the input decays up to the hidden inputEndAmount.
findings.evidence: descriptor field {path: witness.inputStartAmount, label: 'Spend max'}; {path: witness.inputEndAmount, visible: never}. UniswapX DutchDecayLib.decay(DutchInput) reverts if startAmount > endAmount, so the input rises from start to end. The reactor builds TokenPermissions(input.token, input.maxAmount = endAmount). The real cap is shown only as 'Approve amount' (permitted.amount).
findings.fix: Show witness.inputEndAmount as 'Maximum to spend' (tokenAmount, tokenPath witness.inputToken). Drop inputStartAmount or label it 'Starting input amount'.

findings.title: Dutch order intent 'UniswapX Dutch Order' does not say the signer sells one token for another.
findings.evidence: descriptor intent: "UniswapX Dutch Order". The signed order lets the reactor pull the input token and pay the output tokens to the recipients.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Swap tokens with UniswapX". Add an interpolatedIntent such as "Swap up to {permitted.amount} for at least {witness.outputs.[].endAmount}".

findings.title: Dutch order labels say 'Approve' and 'Approval expire', but Permit2 SignatureTransfer sets no standing allowance.
findings.evidence: descriptor labels 'Approve to spender', 'Approve amount', 'Approval expire' on the PermitWitnessTransferFrom primary type. Permit2 SignatureTransfer moves the tokens once and uses the nonce. It sets no allowance.
findings.fix: Rename to 'Order executor', 'Maximum to spend' and 'Signature valid until'.

findings.title: Dutch order output recipients show as raw addresses, so the signer cannot easily see that the recipient is the signer.
findings.evidence: descriptor field {path: recipient, label: 'On Addresses', format: raw} inside witness.outputs.[]. Case 0 shows 0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045.
findings.fix: Use format addressName with types ["eoa","wallet"] and senderAddress so that the signer's own address shows as 'You'.

findings.title: Dutch order spender shows as a raw address, so the signer cannot tell that it is a UniswapX reactor.
findings.evidence: descriptor field {path: spender, label: 'Approve to spender', format: raw}. In cases 0 and 1 the spender is 0xEf1c6E67…BF6B, the mainnet Universal Router address, and the screen does not name it.
findings.fix: Use format addressName with types ["contract"] and sources ["local","ens"] so that wallets can name the reactor.

findings.title: Dutch order 'Minimum amounts to receive' label is also used for fee outputs paid to third parties.
findings.evidence: descriptor witness.outputs.[] field endAmount, label 'Minimum amounts to receive', next to the 'On Addresses' recipient. UniswapX orders can include fee outputs to an interface fee recipient. That amount reaches the fee recipient, not the signer.
findings.fix: Change the label to 'Minimum output' and keep the recipient next to it, or label the recipient 'Paid to'.

findings.title: Dutch order tests use orders the reactor rejects and skip the rising-input path.
findings.evidence: cases 0 and 1: inputStartAmount 2500000000 > inputEndAmount 2400000000 (input must rise). Output startAmount 1e18 < endAmount 1.05e18 (output must fall). Both decay at once (InputAndOutputDecay). permitted.amount 2500000000 ≠ inputEndAmount. The spender is the Universal Router address, not a reactor.
findings.fix: Add valid orders: an exact-input order (output decays down) and an exact-output order (inputStart < inputEnd = permitted.amount). Use a real reactor as spender and info.reactor.

findings.title: Dutch order hides the order deadline and decay window. The order can expire before the shown deadline.
findings.evidence: descriptor: witness.info, witness.decayStartTime and witness.decayEndTime are visible: never. Only the Permit2 'deadline' shows, as 'Approval expire'. The reactor also enforces info.deadline. The bounds still cap what leaves and what arrives.
findings.fix: Optionally show witness.info.deadline as 'Order expires' (date, timestamp).

couldNotCheck: The Permit2 source (0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3) is not in the directory because the Sourcify download failed (429 errors, and chain 9001 is unsupported). I checked the signature transfer and nonce behaviour from what I know of the public Permit2 code, not from these files.

The UniswapX DutchOrderReactor (the spender that uses the witness and decides the decay, how inputs go to the filler, and how outputs are paid) is not in the directory. The input and output decay directions come from what I know of the public UniswapX code.
